<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 46 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cdf09011a77f6d22075f14a9b5626333a56ffdd0` — the merge of head `33e387385df92061c3bfef471a4f5edc485c6bb2` into base `b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cdf09011a77f6d22075f14a9b5626333a56ffdd0 && git checkout cdf09011a77f6d22075f14a9b5626333a56ffdd0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a 33e387385df92061c3bfef471a4f5edc485c6bb2 && git checkout -B drift-repro b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a && git merge --no-ff 33e387385df92061c3bfef471a4f5edc485c6bb2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Local: plugin-auth full suite 274 files / 5301 passed at 44b60330 after the origin/main merge; build + typecheck exit 0; eslint exit 0; two ablations (warn call removed: 4 red; hook call removed: the wiring case red) in the os-dev report (#33313 comment 6884973760); named gates exit 0, check:query-options-erasure NOT MEASURED locally (timed out; CI runs it). Declarations: Clause-② no, Metadata-protocol none.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `44b60330898ed3fe77b7338a004b84d69654b432`

I read the full diff against `main` at `d683e6f3`.

- **One predicate.** `ssoDomainEntriesNotBare` is what `ssoDomainEntryNotBare` iterated before (split on commas, trim, skip blanks, keep entries `ssoDomainEntryHost` rejects), now returning all of them. The refusal names the first one with the same message, status and code, so register and edit answers do not move. The boot report reads the same list, so the two cannot disagree.
- **The boot report reads only and never throws into boot.** It runs on `kernel:ready` as the system, with `fields: ['provider_id', 'domain']` and no write. A missing engine, a missing `find`, an unregistered `sys_sso_provider` or a read error produces a `debug` line and nothing else. It logs one `warn` per provider that has an offending entry, naming the provider and giving the fix (update-provider, then re-verify). This is #33313's ask. The sso.mdx line points operators to it.
- `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`: correct, because the only new behaviour is a log line.
- nit N1: the read passes no `limit`. If the engine applies a default page cap, a deployment with more providers than that cap is only partly reported. Either pass an explicit high limit, or page the read, or say "first N" in the warning.
- nit N2: a refused entry can carry a user part, and the warning echoes the entry as stored. For an entry like `user:secret@acme.com` that puts the text after the colon into the server log. Consider masking the userinfo (`user:***@acme.com`) in the warning only. The refusal message at register is shown to the person who typed it, so it is not affected.

The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head. CI was still running at this head when I read it (22:27Z).

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6` (review#3)

## Review — PASS (delta)

Head-sha: `33e387385df92061c3bfef471a4f5edc485c6bb2`

This reviews the delta `44b60330...33e38738` on my PASS at `44b60330898ed3fe77b7338a004b84d69654b432`. It changes two files and adds one function, `ssoStoredDomainEntryForLog`, plus two tests.

- **N2 is closed.** The function matches `^(scheme://)?[^@/?#]*@`, which is the authority's user part up to the first `@` before any `/`, `?` or `#`, and replaces it with `***`. The match is anchored at the start, so an `@` after a path is left alone (the CONTROL test pins this). Masking applies to the warning text and the `entries` meta only. `findSsoProvidersWithNonBareDomainEntries` still answers the raw entries, and the refusal path is untouched. The ablation shows the mask test bites.
- On N1: the area measured that objectql and driver-sql apply no default page cap to `find`, so the read is unbounded and every provider is reported. Accepted.
- nit (no action needed): a password that itself contains an unencoded `@` keeps whatever follows the first `@`, for example `***@rest@acme.com`. The register refusal already rejects that shape, so such an entry could only come from an old row.

The PASS carries to this head. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6` (review#3)
